key_insight: OpenVLThinkerV2 adapts Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to open-source multimodal models, stabilizing RL-driven fine-tuning across diverse visual tasks while preserving both fine-grained perception and multi-step reasoning.
problem_solved: Overcomes two core obstacles for open-source multimodal generalist models: (1) extreme variance in reward topologies across heterogeneous visual tasks, and (2) the trade-off between fine-grained visual perception and longer multi-step reasoning.
method: Adapt GRPO with task-/group-normalized rewards to reduce variance and make policy updates robust across heterogeneous visual tasks.
Modular perception–reasoning architecture and task-conditioned heads to retain fine visual detail while supporting compositional, multi-step reasoning.
Multi-domain training strategy (task grouping, curriculum, and shared representation learning) plus reward shaping to align objectives across tasks.
impact: Makes RL-based fine-tuning practical for open-source multimodal generalist models, enabling a single model to reliably handle many visual tasks and reducing the engineering cost of balancing perception and reasoning.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram: image encoder → task-conditioned reasoning module → GRPO feedback loop
Heatmap or bar chart showing reward variance per task before vs. after group normalization

Icon grid showing multiple target tasks (VQA, captioning, detection, visual reasoning) to convey generality
paper_title: OpenVLThinkerV2: A Generalist Multimodal Reasoning Model for Multi-domain Visual Tasks
paper_authors: Wenbo Hu, Xin Chen, Yan Gao-Tian, Yihe Deng, Nanyun Peng
